title: A new work order starts with the customer's one representative
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Have an active staff member at the test location with the "Sales Representative" switch on: sales rep A.
  • Use a customer whose one Sales Representative is sales rep A.
  • Open the Work Orders page in a desktop browser at least 1024 pixels wide.
custom_steps:
1. Create a new work order for the customer.
  2. Open the work order's menu.
  3. Click Audit Log.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The new work order shows one "Sales Representative" field reading sales rep A.
  • It is not split.

Step 2:

  • The work order's menu opens.

Step 3:

  • There is no "Sales representative changed" entry for the copied representative.

The Sales By Representative spec, version 28 (12 Oct 2026, S19-R3), still says a new work order opens "Unassigned". Chris Ward ruled on 19 Oct 2026 that the PRD wins (answer 38, quoted below); this case follows PRD version 10, which fills it from the customer.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Splitting Sales Representatives", Confluence 919928833, version 11 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10890, story SV-11268 (Story 4, Give a customer default representatives), story SV-11271 (Story 7, Record representative changes in the work order log)

  • S4-R24: “A new work order for a customer that is not split starts with the customer's representative in its one Sales Representative field. The work order is not split.”
  • S7-R5: “Representatives copied from the customer when a work order is created (S4-R24, S4-R25) write no "Sales representative changed" entry.”

From: Chris Ward's answers to the Splitting Sales Representatives question sheet (answers 1 to 38, 19 Oct 2026; answers 39 and 40, 21 Oct 2026), read 22 Oct 2026

  • Chris Ward's answer 38: “38. (a) The feature spec wins on all three; I'll update the Sales By Representative spec.”
